text: The Π-type Πx:A. B(x), whose return type B(x) varies with the argument value x, is the canonical example of a ___ type — one that mentions a value. The running textbook example is Vector α n.
explanation: A dependent type is a type that depends on a value (e.g. Vector α n depends on the length n). The Π-type Πx:A. B(x) is the dependent function type; when B is constant it collapses to the ordinary arrow A → B. The expected word is 'dependent'.
